subproblem.title: A Lipschitz map with Hoelder derivative on a full-measure set is C^1 with the same Hoelder bound
subproblem.statement: Let n, l >= 0, f : R^n -> R^l, c in R^n, r real, K >= 0, Z a subset of R^n, and M, R, alpha real with M >= 0, R > 0 and alpha > 0. Assume f is K-Lipschitz on the open ball B := B^o_r(c), Z is contained in B, B minus Z is Lebesgue-null, f is differentiable at every point of Z, and hsNorm(Df(x) - Df(y)) <= M (||x - y||/R)^alpha for all x, y in Z, where Df = fderiv f and hsNorm is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Then f is C^1 on B (ContDiffOn R 1 f B) and hsNorm(Df(x) - Df(y)) <= M (||x - y||/R)^alpha for all x, y in B.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (c : Rn n) (r : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (Z : Set (Rn n)) (M R α : ℝ), 0 ≤ M → 0 < R → 0 < α → LipschitzOnWith K f (ball c r) → Z ⊆ ball c r → volume (ball c r \ Z) = 0 → (∀ x ∈ Z, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → (∀ x ∈ Z, ∀ y ∈ Z, hsNorm (fderiv ℝ f x - fderiv ℝ f y) ≤ M * (‖x - y‖ / R) ^ α) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball c r) ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball c r, ∀ y ∈ ball c r, hsNorm (fderiv ℝ f x - fderiv ℝ f y) ≤ M * (‖x - y‖ / R) ^ α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ('By (H), Df restricted to Z is uniformly continuous, and Z is dense (full measure); let g be the unique continuous map with g = Df on Z; g satisfies (H) on the whole ball; ... f is differentiable at every point with fderiv f = g, which is continuous; so f is C^1 and (H) holds on the whole ball'), for an arbitrary Hoelder modulus M (t/R)^alpha. The everywhere-differentiability is the sibling theorem allard52_lipschitz_hasFDerivAt_of_ae.

Notation. B := B^o_r(c) (open ball; if r <= 0, B is empty and both conclusions are trivial). L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm ||.||; it is finite dimensional, hence complete. hsNorm(T) := (sum_{i<n} ||T e_i||^2)^(1/2). kappa(t) := M (t/R)^alpha for t >= 0; since M >= 0, R > 0 and alpha > 0, kappa is continuous and nondecreasing on [0, infinity) with kappa(0) = 0. Df(x) := fderiv f x.

1. Hilbert-Schmidt versus operator norm. For T in L and v in R^n, write v = sum_i v_i e_i with ||v||^2 = sum_i v_i^2. Then ||T v|| <= sum_i |v_i| ||T e_i|| <= (sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2) (sum_i ||T e_i||^2)^(1/2) = ||v|| hsNorm(T) (Cauchy-Schwarz for finite sums). Hence ||T|| <= hsNorm(T) (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). Moreover hsNorm is continuous on L (square root of a finite sum of squared norms of the continuous evaluations T -> T e_i).

2. Density. Z is dense in B: let x be in B and epsilon > 0; W := B^o_epsilon(x) cap B is open and nonempty (it contains x), so L^n(W) > 0. If W did not meet Z, W would be contained in B minus Z, which has measure 0; contradiction. Hence B is contained in the closure of Z, and for every x in B the filter of neighbourhoods of x within Z (nhdsWithin x Z) is nontrivial.

3. Limits along Z. Let x be in B. For eta > 0 and z, z' in Z cap B^o_eta(x): ||Df(z) - Df(z')|| <= hsNorm(Df(z) - Df(z')) <= kappa(||z - z'||) <= kappa(2 eta) (step 1, hypothesis, monotonicity of kappa). Since kappa(2 eta) -> 0 as eta -> 0+, the image of nhdsWithin x Z under Df is a Cauchy filter on the complete space L, hence converges. Define g := extendFrom Z Df (the limit of Df along nhdsWithin x Z). Then for every x in B, Df(z) -> g(x) as z -> x within Z (extendFrom_eq), and g is continuous on B (continuousOn_extendFrom, using step 2). If x is in Z, then ||Df(z) - Df(x)|| <= kappa(||z - x||) -> 0 as z -> x, so g(x) = Df(x) (limits in the Hausdorff space L are unique).

4. Hoelder bound for g. Let x, y be in B. Along the nontrivial product filter (nhdsWithin x Z) x (nhdsWithin y Z): Df(z) - Df(z') -> g(x) - g(y), hence hsNorm(Df(z) - Df(z')) -> hsNorm(g(x) - g(y)) (step 1, continuity of hsNorm); and kappa(||z - z'||) -> kappa(||x - y||) (continuity of the norm and of kappa). Since z, z' are eventually in Z, the hypothesis gives hsNorm(Df(z) - Df(z')) <= kappa(||z - z'||) eventually, and passing to the limit (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto): hsNorm(g(x) - g(y)) <= kappa(||x - y||).

5. Differentiability everywhere. For x in Z, f is differentiable at x, so f has Frechet derivative Df(x) = g(x) at x (step 3). Hence the set of x in B at which f does not have derivative g(x) is contained in B minus Z, which is L^n-null; that is, for L^n-a.e. x: x in B implies HasFDerivAt f (g x) x. Since f is K-Lipschitz on B and g is continuous on B (step 3), the sibling theorem allard52_lipschitz_hasFDerivAt_of_ae (with this f, g, c, r, K) gives HasFDerivAt f (g x) x for every x in B. Consequently f is differentiable on B and fderiv f x = g(x) for every x in B.

6. C^1. B is open, f is differentiable on B, and fderiv f coincides on B with g, which is continuous on B (step 3); so fderiv f is continuous on B (ContinuousOn.congr). By contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen with order 0 + 1 = 1, f is C^1 on B: ContDiffOn R 1 f B. (In this Mathlib the right side of that equivalence consists of DifferentiableOn f B, the clause (0 = ω → AnalyticOn f B), where ω is the analytic smoothness order and the clause holds trivially since 0 ≠ ω, and ContDiffOn 0 (fderiv f) B, which is continuity of fderiv f on B by contDiffOn_zero.)

7. Hoelder bound for Df. For x, y in B, by steps 5 and 4: hsNorm(fderiv f x - fderiv f y) = hsNorm(g(x) - g(y)) <= M (||x - y||/R)^alpha.
proof_key_steps: Z is dense in B since B minus Z is null and nonempty open sets have positive measure
The Hoelder bound makes Df Cauchy along Z, so g := extendFrom Z Df is continuous on B and equals Df on Z
Passing to the limit along Z x Z gives the Hoelder bound for g on all of B
Sibling allard52_lipschitz_hasFDerivAt_of_ae gives fderiv f = g on B, hence C^1 (contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen) and the Hoelder bound

audit.reason: The prose and independently usable type agree. Full measure gives density; the Hölder modulus and operator-norm comparison give Cauchy limits and a continuous extension preserving the exact bound. Its sole declared dependency supplies everywhere differentiability, after which the open-set C¹ criterion applies. This dependency is correctly directed, and the proof is complete and non-circular.
